description: Region-local CUDA graph around the proj_cqr CholeskyQR2 sub-chain (Gram-bmm -> add_shifted_diag -> potrf -> trsm, x2 passes) for shape 11 + the low-rank CQR2 shapes: a sibling measured ~8.5-10ms of proj_cqr's 20ms is HOST-DISPATCH GAP across ~14 dependent launches (plus cuSOLVER's ~700 tiny internal potrf kernels at small batch), and explicitly found the whole-pipeline graph refutation (92% GPU-busy) does NOT bind this region in isolation where the gap is ~45% of the stage. Mechanism: capture the fixed-topology CQR2 launch sequence as an explicit-node CUDA graph (cudaGraphCreate/AddKernelNode/Instantiate, none contain 'stream') launched via cudaGraphLaunch(exec,NULL) on the default stream, replaying the real potrf/trsm kernels; shape-keyed graph cache; data-dependent gate/fallback stays outside the graph. Targets launch-overhead / host-device sync; keep the residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

Parent baseline re-measured (fork dcb7eea51). geomean 27580us. shape11=81116us; CQR2-region idle gap MEASURED at 0.90ms/12.63ms (7.1%), NOT ~8.5ms -- region 93% GPU-busy, most idle is topk boundary. Building region-local graph next.

Built explicit-node CUDA graph module (cudaGraphCreate/AddKernelNode/Instantiate + cudaGraphLaunch(exec,NULL); NO stream substring). Own batched Gram/shift/Cholesky/trsm as explicit nodes, shape-keyed cache. Graph output matches library CQR2 (max|diff|3.1e-4) but replay=156.6ms vs library=22.9ms = 6.8x SLOWER even with zero dispatch gap -- own single-CTA potrf/trsm occupancy-bound. Graph OFF, no regression. geomean 27578us.

Higher-occupancy multi-CTA batched trsm (NCTA CTAs/matrix, L from HBM/L2, tiny SMEM). vs cuBLAS trsm=6.96ms: ncta=1 26.2ms, ncta>=2 22.6ms (correct max|err|1e-5). Occupancy fix recovers only ~14%; still 3.25x slower than cuBLAS (blocked L-tile reuse a per-row HBM-read forward-sub cannot match). Graph OFF, geomean 27541us, 39/39 valid.

Built the region-local explicit-node CUDA graph (cudaGraphCreate/AddKernelNode/Instantiate + cudaGraphLaunch(exec,NULL); NO 'stream' substring, verified) around the CQR2 sub-chain and MEASURED it end-to-end. Three findings, all committed (graph OFF, 39/39 valid, geomean 27541-27580us = parent, no shape regresses): (1) The proj_cqr dispatch gap is NOT ~8.5ms -- nsys on the parent shows the CQR2 region is 93% GPU-busy: wall 12.63ms, idle only 0.90ms (7.1%), and most of that 0.9ms is the topk boundary leak, not inter-op gaps (potrf/trsm gaps are ~3us = min launch latency). Same holds for the low-rank CQR2 (shape 12, batch 60, k=384): region wall 3.44ms vs isolated 2-pass busy 3.54ms => gap ~0. The CQR2 region is library-GPU-bound, not dispatch-bound. (2) Library calls (cuSOLVER potrf, cuBLAS trsm) CANNOT enter an explicit-node graph -- they expose no kernel-node API and the only capture route uses the banned begin-capture call. So the graph must use OWN kernels. (3) Own batched potrf/trsm as explicit graph nodes are 3.25-7.7x SLOWER than the libraries EVEN AT ZERO dispatch gap: t2 full graph replay=156.6ms vs library CQR2=22.9ms (6.8x); t3 higher-occupancy multi-CTA trsm (L from L2, tiny SMEM, full occupancy) recovers only ~14% (26->22.6ms) but is still 3.25x slower than cuBLAS trsm=6.96ms; own gram+shift+chol=39.2ms vs library 5.06ms (7.7x, occupancy-bound at 176KB resident triangle -> 1 CTA/SM). CONCLUSION for this brief: the proj_cqr dispatch gap is LIBRARY-LOCKED, not graph-removable -- the ~0.9ms of removable gap is worth far less than the >=130ms penalty of replacing the library kernels with graphable ones. The graph mechanism is proven correct (output matches library to max|diff|3.1e-4) and left in place OFF. OPEN DIRECTIONS to surface (OFF this brief): the REAL removable idle in shape 11 is ~4ms in the ns_sign stage (t=2-20.3ms is 22.2% idle, ~213us gaps BETWEEN consecutive Newton-Schulz bmm/baddbmm iterations) -- a bigger lever than proj_cqr's 0.9ms, but it's LIBRARY-GEMM-locked too (baddbmm/bmm can't be explicit nodes). Worth a manager brief on WHY those 213us NS inter-iteration gaps exist (kernel-config/launch-serialization on the 640x512x512 batch) and whether a fused custom NS-step kernel (one launch doing X@X@X per iter, batched, tensor-core) would both cut the GEMM count and remove the gap. Also: my multi-CTA trsm at 3.25x could be pushed with L-tile SMEM staging (blocked forward-sub reusing L tiles across RHS like cuBLAS) -- didn't reach a blocked-SMEM variant; and k>320 low-rank CQR2 (k=384/608/640) was never graphable with the current CQRG_TRSM_KMAX=320 kernels.
